title: Contributing to tidylearn
text: tidylearn follows standard R package convention described R Packages (2e), §21.2: Released versions CRAN use three components: X.Y.Z (e.g. 0.5.0). Development versions — state package CRAN releases — append fourth component .9000 last released version. CRAN 0.5.0, main branch reads Version: 0.5.0.9000 entire time working toward next release. .9000 suffix signal says “dev build, CRAN release.” maintainer ready submit next release CRAN, version bumped 0.6.0 (dropping .9000), submitted, immediately bumped back 0.6.0.9000 main next dev cycle. ’ll sometimes see .9001, .9002, etc. used mark meaningful dev milestones, .9000 alone default fine ordinary PRs.

title: Contributing to tidylearn
text: Follow surrounding code. package leans tidyverse conventions: snake_case function variable names. exception name mirrors argument wrapped package — e.g. n.trees (gbm), minPts (dbscan), B (cluster::clusGap) — keeps package’s spelling interface stays familiar. .lintr allows dotted.case camelCase reason; .lintr parsed strict DCF carry comment, hence note. <- (=) assignment. Exported functions need roxygen documentation @param, @return, @examples, @export. lintr::lint_package() report issues. Install package first (R CMD INSTALL . devtools::install()) object_usage_linter can resolve namespace — otherwise reports spurious “visible global function definition” lints package’s internal functions.

code: dir <- tempfile(pattern = "tl_vignette_") dir.create(dir) write.csv(iris[1:50, ], file.path(dir, "jan.csv"), row.names = FALSE) write.csv(iris[51:100, ], file.path(dir, "feb.csv"), row.names = FALSE) write.csv(iris[101:150, ], file.path(dir, "mar.csv"), row.names = FALSE)  # Read all CSVs from the directory all_data <- tl_read_dir(dir, format = "csv", .quiet = TRUE) nrow(all_data) #> [1] 150 table(all_data$source_file) #>  #> feb.csv jan.csv mar.csv  #>      50      50      50 # Filter with a regex pattern subset <- tl_read_dir(dir, pattern = "^(jan|feb)", .quiet = TRUE) nrow(subset) #> [1] 100 data <- tl_read("data/monthly_exports/")

title: Data Ingestion with tidylearn
text: Combining tl_read() rest tidylearn gives complete workflow raw data published results:
code: # 1. Ingest tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv") write.csv(iris, tmp, row.names = FALSE) data <- tl_read(tmp, .quiet = TRUE)  # CSV files lose factor information, so convert character columns as needed data <- data %>% mutate(Species = as.factor(Species))  # 2. Split split <- tl_split(data, prop = 0.7, stratify = "Species", seed = 42)  # 3. Model model <- tl_model(split$train, Species ~ ., method = "forest")  # 4. Evaluate eval_result <- tl_evaluate(model, new_data = split$test) eval_result #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   metric   value #>   <chr>    <dbl> #> 1 accuracy 0.956

title: Diagnostics
text: model fits model use. functions answer four questions: assumptions hold? tl_check_assumptions() observations drove fit? tl_influence_measures(), tl_detect_outliers() difference two models real? tl_compare_cv(), tl_test_model_difference() interactions modelled? tl_test_interactions(), tl_interaction_effects() tl_explore() runs unsupervised sweep dataset model . use linear model throughout, assumption checking teeth.
code: model <- tl_model(mtcars, mpg ~ wt + hp + disp, method = "linear")

title: Diagnostics
text: tl_check_assumptions() runs six checks returns verdict . entry carries test run, verdict, . Nothing pass/fail gate — recommendation prompt, instruction. compact table every check: disp correlating wt hp drives VIF , kind thing invisible coefficient table.
code: assumptions <- tl_check_assumptions(model, verbose = FALSE) names(assumptions) #> [1] "linearity"         "independence"      "homoscedasticity"  #> [4] "normality"         "multicollinearity" "outliers"          #> [7] "overall" assumptions$overall #> $status #> [1] "5 assumption(s) appear to be violated. See details." #>  #> $n_checked #> [1] 6 #>  #> $n_violated #> [1] 5 #>  #> $n_satisfied #> [1] 1 assumptions$normality #> $assumption #> [1] "Normality of Residuals" #>  #> $check #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $details #> [1] "Shapiro-Wilk test p-value: 0.033" #>  #> $recommendation #> [1] "Residuals may not be normally distributed. Consider transformations or robust regression." assumptions$multicollinearity #> $assumption #> [1] "No Multicollinearity" #>  #> $check #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $details #> [1] "Maximum VIF: 7.3245" #>  #> $recommendation #> [1] "Multicollinearity detected. Consider removing or combining highly correlated predictors." checks <- c("linearity", "independence", "homoscedasticity",             "normality", "multicollinearity", "outliers")  data.frame(   assumption = vapply(checks, function(x) assumptions[[x]]$assumption,                       character(1)),   holds = vapply(checks, function(x) isTRUE(assumptions[[x]]$check),                  logical(1)),   detail = vapply(checks, function(x) assumptions[[x]]$details, character(1)),   row.names = NULL ) #>                assumption holds #> 1               Linearity FALSE #> 2            Independence FALSE #> 3        Homoscedasticity  TRUE #> 4  Normality of Residuals FALSE #> 5    No Multicollinearity FALSE #> 6 No Influential Outliers FALSE #>                                                                detail #> 1 RESET-style test on powers of the fitted values: p-value = 0.001944 #> 2                                     Durbin-Watson statistic: 1.3673 #> 3                                  Breusch-Pagan test p-value: 0.8143 #> 4                                    Shapiro-Wilk test p-value: 0.033 #> 5                                                 Maximum VIF: 7.3245 #> 6                                 4 influential observations detected

title: Diagnostics
text: difference single held-score evidence. tl_compare_cv() scores several fitted models folds. Per-fold scores kept well, makes test possible:
code: simple <- tl_model(mtcars, mpg ~ wt, method = "linear") full <- tl_model(mtcars, mpg ~ wt + hp + disp, method = "linear") tree <- tl_model(mtcars, mpg ~ wt + hp + disp, method = "tree")  cv <- tl_compare_cv(   mtcars,   models = list(simple = simple, full = full, tree = tree),   folds = 5,   metrics = c("rmse", "rsq") )  names(cv) #> [1] "fold_metrics" "summary" cv$summary #> # A tibble: 6 × 6 #>   model  metric mean_value sd_value min_value max_value #>   <chr>  <chr>       <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 full   rmse        2.93     0.708     2.17      3.93  #> 2 full   rsq         0.612    0.248     0.262     0.859 #> 3 simple rmse        3.09     0.720     1.82      3.59  #> 4 simple rsq         0.530    0.414    -0.169     0.820 #> 5 tree   rmse        4.42     1.60      2.21      6.58  #> 6 tree   rsq         0.148    0.527    -0.501     0.767 head(cv$fold_metrics) #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   metric value  fold model  #>   <chr>  <dbl> <int> <chr>  #> 1 rmse   3.35      1 simple #> 2 rsq    0.820     1 simple #> 3 rmse   1.82      2 simple #> 4 rsq    0.808     2 simple #> 5 rmse   3.29      3 simple #> 6 rsq    0.481     3 simple

title: Diagnostics
text: tl_test_model_difference() compares model baseline using per-fold scores. five folds little power, treat non-significant result “folds separate models” rather evidence equivalent. test = "wilcox.test" drops normality assumption, matters small fold counts loss power costs .

text: Logistic regression handles two-class problems, take binary subset iris . three classes use "tree", "forest", "svm" "nn". Predictions come back tibble .pred column. .pred contains depends type: "class" gives predicted label, "prob" gives one column per class. Note default type = "response" means different things across methods — probabilities logistic regression, class labels trees forests. Ask type = "class" explicitly want labels, let tl_evaluate() handle :
code: # versicolor and virginica overlap, so this is a real classification # problem -- setosa is linearly separable from the other two, which makes # logistic regression fail to converge iris_binary <- iris %>%   filter(Species %in% c("versicolor", "virginica")) %>%   mutate(Species = droplevels(Species))  model_logistic <- tl_model(iris_binary, Species ~ ., method = "logistic") print(model_logistic) #> tidylearn Model #> =============== #> Paradigm: supervised  #> Method: logistic  #> Task: Classification  #> Formula: Species ~ .  #>  #> Training observations: 100 # Predicted class labels predictions <- predict(model_logistic, type = "class") head(predictions) #> # A tibble: 6 × 1 #>   .pred      #>   <fct>      #> 1 versicolor #> 2 versicolor #> 3 versicolor #> 4 versicolor #> 5 versicolor #> 6 versicolor # Class probabilities head(predict(model_logistic, type = "prob")) #> # A tibble: 6 × 2 #>   versicolor virginica #>        <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1      1.000 0.0000117 #> 2      1.000 0.0000486 #> 3      0.999 0.00120   #> 4      1.000 0.0000422 #> 5      0.999 0.00141   #> 6      1.000 0.000102 tl_evaluate(model_logistic, metrics = c("accuracy", "f1")) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   metric   value #>   <chr>    <dbl> #> 1 accuracy  0.98 #> 2 f1        0.98

# Split data for fair comparison split <- tl_split(iris, prop = 0.7, stratify = "Species", seed = 123)  # Model with original features model_original <- tl_model(split$train, Species ~ ., method = "forest") eval_original <- tl_evaluate(model_original, new_data = split$test)  # Model with PCA features reduced_train <- tl_reduce_dimensions(split$train,                                       response = "Species",                                       method = "pca",                                       n_components = 3)  model_pca <- tl_model(reduced_train$data, Species ~ ., method = "forest")  # The test set must be projected through the PCA fitted on the training # data -- refitting PCA on the test set would leak information test_transformed <- predict(   reduced_train$reduction_model,   new_data = split$test %>% select(-Species) ) test_transformed$Species <- split$test$Species  eval_pca <- tl_evaluate(model_pca, new_data = test_transformed)  # Compare results acc <- function(x) round(x$value[x$metric == "accuracy"] * 100, 1) n_original <- ncol(split$train) - 1 n_reduced <- sum(grepl("^PC", names(reduced_train$data))) cat("Original features:", n_original, "->", acc(eval_original), "%
") #> Original features: 4 -> 93.3 % cat("PCA features:", n_reduced, "->", acc(eval_pca), "%
") #> PCA features: 3 -> 91.1 % cat("Feature reduction:",     round((1 - n_reduced / n_original) * 100, 1), "%
") #> Feature reduction: 25 %

code: # Compare models with and without cluster features split_comp <- tl_split(iris, prop = 0.7, stratify = "Species", seed = 42)  # Without cluster features model_no_cluster <- tl_model(split_comp$train, Species ~ ., method = "forest") preds_no_cluster <- predict(model_no_cluster, new_data = split_comp$test) acc_no_cluster <- mean(preds_no_cluster$.pred == split_comp$test$Species)  # With cluster features train_clustered <- tl_add_cluster_features(split_comp$train,                                            response = "Species",                                            method = "kmeans",                                            k = 3) model_with_cluster <- tl_model(train_clustered, Species ~ ., method = "forest")  # Need to get cluster model for test data cluster_model <- attr(train_clustered, "cluster_model") test_clusters <- predict(cluster_model, new_data = split_comp$test[, -5]) test_clustered <- split_comp$test test_clustered$cluster_kmeans <- as.factor(test_clusters$cluster)  preds_with_cluster <- predict(model_with_cluster, new_data = test_clustered) acc_with_cluster <- mean(preds_with_cluster$.pred == split_comp$test$Species)  cat("Without cluster features:", round(acc_no_cluster * 100, 1), "%\n") #> Without cluster features: 95.6 % cat("With cluster features:", round(acc_with_cluster * 100, 1), "%\n") #> With cluster features: 93.3 %

code: # Use only 10% of labels set.seed(123) labeled_indices <- sample(nrow(iris), size = 15)  # 15 of 150 labelled  # supervised_method defaults to "tree". Named here because a forest is # the better fit for propagated labels: the propagation step introduces # noise, and averaging over trees absorbs more of it than one tree does. model_semi <- tl_semisupervised(iris, Species ~ .,                                 labeled_indices = labeled_indices,                                 cluster_method = "kmeans",                                 supervised_method = "forest")  print(model_semi) #> tidylearn Model #> =============== #> Paradigm: supervised  #> Method: forest  #> Task: Classification  #> Formula: Species ~ .  #>  #> Training observations: 150 # Check how labels were propagated label_mapping <- model_semi$semisupervised_info$label_mapping print(label_mapping) #> # A tibble: 3 × 2 #>   cluster cluster_label #>     <int> <chr>         #> 1       1 virginica     #> 2       2 versicolor    #> 3       3 setosa # Evaluate against the true labels preds_semi <- predict(model_semi, new_data = iris, type = "class") accuracy_semi <- mean(preds_semi$.pred == iris$Species)  cat("Accuracy with only", length(labeled_indices), "labels:",     round(accuracy_semi * 100, 1), "%\n") #> Accuracy with only 15 labels: 90 % labeled_pct <- round(   length(labeled_indices) / nrow(iris) * 100, 1 ) cat("Proportion of data labeled:", labeled_pct, "%\n") #> Proportion of data labeled: 10 %

code: # Step 1: Split data workflow_split <- tl_split(iris, prop = 0.7, stratify = "Species", seed = 42)  # Step 2: Reduce dimensions workflow_reduced <- tl_reduce_dimensions(workflow_split$train,                                          response = "Species",                                          method = "pca",                                          n_components = 3)  # Step 3: Add cluster features to reduced data workflow_clustered <- tl_add_cluster_features(workflow_reduced$data,                                               response = "Species",                                               method = "kmeans",                                               k = 3)  # Step 4: Train final model workflow_model <- tl_model(workflow_clustered, Species ~ ., method = "forest")  print(workflow_model) #> tidylearn Model #> =============== #> Paradigm: supervised  #> Method: forest  #> Task: Classification  #> Formula: Species ~ .  #>  #> Training observations: 105 # Transform test data through same pipeline # 1. Apply PCA transformation test_pca <- predict(workflow_reduced$reduction_model,                     new_data = workflow_split$test[, -5]) test_pca$Species <- workflow_split$test$Species  # 2. Get cluster assignments. The cluster model was fitted on the PC # columns; predict() matches new_data to those columns by name and # errors on a mismatch rather than assigning against the wrong ones. cluster_model_wf <- attr(workflow_clustered, "cluster_model") test_clusters_wf <- predict(cluster_model_wf, new_data = test_pca) test_pca$cluster_kmeans <- as.factor(test_clusters_wf$cluster)  # 3. code: # Simulate credit data set.seed(42) n <- 500 credit_data <- data.frame(   age = rnorm(n, 40, 12),   income = rnorm(n, 50000, 20000),   debt_ratio = runif(n, 0, 0.5),   credit_score = rnorm(n, 700, 100),   years_employed = rpois(n, 5) )  # Create target variable (default risk) credit_data$default <- factor(   ifelse(     credit_data$debt_ratio > 0.4 & credit_data$credit_score < 650,     "Yes", "No"   ) )  # Split data credit_split <- tl_split(   credit_data, prop = 0.7, stratify = "default", seed = 123 ) # Strategy 1: Add customer segments as features credit_clustered <- tl_add_cluster_features(credit_split$train,                                             response = "default",                                             method = "kmeans",                                             k = 4)  model_credit <- tl_model(credit_clustered, default ~ ., method = "forest")  # Transform test data cluster_model_credit <- attr(credit_clustered, "cluster_model") test_clusters_credit <- predict(cluster_model_credit,                                 new_data = credit_split$test[, -6]) test_credit <- credit_split$test test_credit$cluster_kmeans <- as.factor(test_clusters_credit$cluster)  preds_credit <- predict(model_credit, new_data = test_credit) accuracy_credit <- mean(preds_credit$.pred == credit_split$test$default)  cat("Credit Risk Model Accuracy:", round(accuracy_credit * 100, 1), "%\n") #> Credit Risk Model Accuracy: 100 %

title: Supervised Learning with tidylearn
text: Let’s create binary classification problem iris dataset:
code: # Create binary classification dataset. setosa is linearly separable from # the other two species, and logistic regression has no finite maximum # likelihood estimate on separable data -- glm() fits, warns that the # algorithm did not converge, and returns coefficients that diverged. # versicolor and virginica overlap, so this is a real classification # problem. Even here, a 70% split of 100 rows is separable at some seeds; # this one is not. iris_binary <- iris %>%   filter(Species %in% c("versicolor", "virginica")) %>%   mutate(Species = droplevels(Species))  # Split data split <- tl_split(iris_binary, prop = 0.7, stratify = "Species", seed = 42)

title: Supervised Learning with tidylearn
text: type argument controls .pred holds. matters: default "response" returns probabilities logistic regression class labels trees, forests SVMs. Ask type = "class" want labels regardless method. tl_evaluate() resolves — always scores class labels, computes whichever metrics ask :
code: # Train logistic regression model_logistic <- tl_model(split$train, Species ~ ., method = "logistic") print(model_logistic) #> tidylearn Model #> =============== #> Paradigm: supervised  #> Method: logistic  #> Task: Classification  #> Formula: Species ~ .  #>  #> Training observations: 70 # Predicted labels preds_logistic <- predict(model_logistic, new_data = split$test, type = "class") head(preds_logistic) #> # A tibble: 6 × 1 #>   .pred      #>   <fct>      #> 1 versicolor #> 2 versicolor #> 3 versicolor #> 4 versicolor #> 5 versicolor #> 6 versicolor # Class probabilities head(predict(model_logistic, new_data = split$test, type = "prob")) #> # A tibble: 6 × 2 #>   versicolor  virginica #>        <dbl>      <dbl> #> 1      1.000 0.0000690  #> 2      1.000 0.0000917  #> 3      0.999 0.00101    #> 4      1.000 0.00000874 #> 5      1.000 0.000208   #> 6      0.952 0.0480 tl_evaluate(   model_logistic,   new_data = split$test,   metrics = c("accuracy", "precision", "recall", "f1", "auc") ) #> # A tibble: 5 × 2 #>   metric    value #>   <chr>     <dbl> #> 1 accuracy  0.867 #> 2 precision 1     #> 3 recall    0.733 #> 4 f1        0.846 #> 5 auc       0.991

what: Replaying Preprocessing on the Test Set
title: Supervised Learning with tidylearn
text: model trained scaled features expects scaled inputs prediction time. tl_prepare_data() keeps parameters learned, transformation can replayed test set — applying training centre scale, never recomputing test data: Skipping step predicting raw test data common quiet mistake — model still returns predictions, just wrong. multi-step preprocessing, tl_pipeline() handles bookkeeping : tl_predict_pipeline() replays training preprocessing automatically.
code: # Complete workflow example final_split <- tl_split(iris, prop = 0.7, stratify = "Species", seed = 42)  final_prep <- tl_prepare_data(   final_split$train, Species ~ .,   scale_method = "standardize" ) #> Scaling numeric features using method: standardize final_model <- tl_model(final_prep$data, Species ~ ., method = "forest") scaling <- final_prep$preprocessing_steps$scaling$scaling_params  final_test <- final_split$test for (col in names(scaling)) {   final_test[[col]] <-     (final_test[[col]] - scaling[[col]]$mean) / scaling[[col]]$sd }  final_preds <- predict(final_model, new_data = final_test) accuracy <- mean(final_preds$.pred == final_split$test$Species) cat("Test Accuracy:", round(accuracy * 100, 1), "%\n") #> Test Accuracy: 95.6 %

title: Tuning and Pipelines
text: tl_model() fits one model hyperparameters name. Two families build : Tuning searches space hyperparameters returns model fitted winner. tl_tune_grid() walks every combination; tl_tune_random() samples ranges. Pipelines bundle preprocessing, set models, evaluation scheme one object can run, save, reload, predict . two compose: tune find settings, put winning settings pipeline whole recipe reproducible.

title: Tuning and Pipelines
text: tl_tune_grid() takes named list candidate values, one entry per hyperparameter, cross-validates every combination. comes back ordinary tidylearn model, already fitted winning settings, everything normally model still works: search attached "tuning_results" attribute: winning values reach underlying fit, just report:
code: tuned_tree <- tl_tune_grid(   iris, Species ~ .,   method = "tree",   param_grid = list(cp = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.1), minsplit = c(5, 20)),   folds = 3,   verbose = FALSE ) print(tuned_tree) #> tidylearn Model #> =============== #> Paradigm: supervised  #> Method: tree  #> Task: Classification  #> Formula: Species ~ .  #>  #> Training observations: 150 tuning <- attr(tuned_tree, "tuning_results") names(tuning) #> [1] "param_grid"  "results"     "best_params" "best_metric" "metric"      #> [6] "maximize" tuning$results #>   mean_metric    cp minsplit #> 1   0.9666667 0.001        5 #> 2   0.9466667 0.001       20 #> 3   0.9666667 0.010        5 #> 4   0.9466667 0.010       20 #> 5   0.9466667 0.100        5 #> 6   0.9466667 0.100       20 # The settings that won, and the score they won with tuning$best_params #> $cp #> [1] 0.001 #>  #> $minsplit #> [1] 5 tuning$best_metric #> [1] 0.9666667 tuned_tree$fit$control$cp #> [1] 0.001

code: tuned_reg <- tl_tune_grid(   mtcars, mpg ~ .,   method = "forest",   param_grid = list(mtry = c(2, 4), ntree = c(100, 300)),   folds = 3,   metric = "rmse",   verbose = FALSE )  attr(tuned_reg, "tuning_results")$best_params #> $mtry #> [1] 4 #>  #> $ntree #> [1] 100

Without , two runs sample different points can pick different winners.

title: Tuning and Pipelines
text: pipeline records preprocessing, models fit, evaluate . Building work; tl_run_pipeline() . Anything leave preprocessing evaluation takes default, partial list fine. unrecognised name error rather step quietly nothing.
code: split <- tl_split(iris, prop = 0.7, stratify = "Species", seed = 42)  pipe <- tl_pipeline(   split$train, Species ~ .,   preprocessing = list(standardize = TRUE, dummy_encode = FALSE),   models = list(     tree = list(method = "tree"),     forest = list(method = "forest", ntree = 300)   ),   evaluation = list(     validation = "cv",     cv_folds = 3,     metrics = c("accuracy", "f1"),     best_metric = "accuracy"   ) )  print(pipe) #> Tidylearn Pipeline #> ================= #> Formula: Species ~ .  #> Data: 105 observations, 5 variables #> Preprocessing: impute_missing, standardize  #> Models: tree, forest  #> Evaluation:  cv (3 folds) #> Metrics: accuracy, f1  #> Best metric: accuracy tl_pipeline(split$train, Species ~ .,             preprocessing = list(scale_method = "standardize")) #> Error: #> ! Unknown preprocessing step(s): scale_method. Available steps: impute_missing, standardize, dummy_encode.

title: Tuning and Pipelines
text: tl_get_best_model() returns model won best_metric:
code: run <- tl_run_pipeline(pipe, verbose = FALSE)  names(run$models) #> [1] "tree"   "forest" print(run) #> Tidylearn Pipeline #> ================= #> Formula: Species ~ .  #> Data: 105 observations, 5 variables #> Preprocessing: impute_missing, standardize  #> Models: tree, forest  #> Evaluation:  cv (3 folds) #> Metrics: accuracy, f1  #> Best metric: accuracy  #>  #> Results #> ======= #> Best model: tree  #> Performance: #>   tree: accuracy = 0.9714 (best) #>   forest: accuracy = 0.9714 best <- tl_get_best_model(run) best$spec$method #> [1] "tree"

title: Tuning and Pipelines
text: reason use pipeline rather bare model. Predicting raw new data replays preprocessing pipeline learned run, applying training centre scale rather recomputing new rows. Omit model_name predict best model.
code: preds <- tl_predict_pipeline(run, new_data = split$test, model_name = "forest") head(preds) #> # A tibble: 6 × 1 #>   .pred  #>   <fct>  #> 1 setosa #> 2 setosa #> 3 setosa #> 4 setosa #> 5 setosa #> 6 setosa mean(preds$.pred == split$test$Species) #> [1] 0.9333333

code: path <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") tl_save_pipeline(run, path)  reloaded <- tl_load_pipeline(path) names(reloaded$models) #> [1] "tree"   "forest" # Predictions survive the round trip, preprocessing included reloaded_preds <- tl_predict_pipeline(   reloaded, new_data = split$test, model_name = "forest" ) identical(reloaded_preds$.pred, preds$.pred) #> [1] TRUE

title: Tuning and Pipelines
text: Tuning tells settings; pipeline holds alongside preprocessing produced .
code: tuned <- tl_tune_grid(   split$train, Species ~ .,   method = "forest",   param_grid = list(mtry = c(2, 3), ntree = c(100, 300)),   folds = 3,   verbose = FALSE )  best_params <- attr(tuned, "tuning_results")$best_params best_params #> $mtry #> [1] 2 #>  #> $ntree #> [1] 100 final <- tl_pipeline(   split$train, Species ~ .,   models = list(     forest = c(list(method = "forest"), best_params)   ),   evaluation = list(cv_folds = 3, metrics = "accuracy",                     best_metric = "accuracy") )  final_run <- tl_run_pipeline(final, verbose = FALSE) final_preds <- tl_predict_pipeline(final_run, new_data = split$test)  mean(final_preds$.pred == split$test$Species) #> [1] 0.9333333

Unlike PCA can work distance matrix, including non-Euclidean ones.  method also takes "metric" "nonmetric" (via smacof), "sammon" "kruskal". last two minimise stress function dividing observed distances, need every pairwise distance strictly positive. iris contains one duplicated row, enough stop : Drop duplicates run: Stress number check reading anything non-metric layout: 0.05 picture faithful rendering distances, 0.2 decoration.

what: tidylearn: A Unified Tidy Interface to R's Machine Learning Ecosystem — tidylearn-package
title: tidylearn: A Unified Tidy Interface to R's Machine Learning Ecosystem — tidylearn-package
text: Provides unified tidyverse-compatible interface R's machine learning ecosystem - data ingestion model publishing. tl_read() family reads data files ('CSV', 'Excel', 'Parquet', 'JSON'), databases ('SQLite', 'PostgreSQL', 'MySQL', 'BigQuery'), cloud sources ('S3', 'GitHub', 'Kaggle'). tl_model() function wraps established implementations 'glmnet', 'randomForest', 'xgboost', 'e1071', 'rpart', 'gbm', 'nnet', 'cluster', 'dbscan', others consistent function signatures tidy tibble output. Results flow unified 'ggplot2'-based visualization optional formatted 'gt' tables via tl_table() family. underlying algorithms unchanged; 'tidylearn' simply makes easier use together. Access raw model objects via $fit slot supervised method, $fit$model unsupervised one. Methods include random forests Breiman (2001) doi:10.1023/:1010933404324 , LASSO regression Tibshirani (1996) doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1996.tb02080.x , elastic net Zou Hastie (2005) doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2005.00503.x , support vector machines Cortes Vapnik (1995) doi:10.1007/BF00994018 , gradient boosting Friedman (2001) doi:10.1214/aos/1013203451 .

title: tidylearn: A Unified Tidy Interface to R's Machine Learning Ecosystem — tidylearn-package
text: tidylearn wraps established R machine learning packages behind one consistent interface. main entry points : tl_read Read data files, databases cloud sources tidy tibble. tl_model Fit supported supervised unsupervised method. tl_evaluate Score fitted model. tl_table Render results formatted gt tables. tl_auto_ml Search across methods automatically. Every fitted model keeps underlying package's object $fit slot, package-specific functionality remains available. See vignette("getting-started", package = "tidylearn") walkthrough.

Controls models attempted whether cross-validation used evaluation. budget checked model fits, – model starts training runs completion R safely interrupt C-level code (e.g. randomForest, xgboost, e1071). budget shapes workflow: 30s: fast models attempted (tree, logistic/linear). Cross-validation skipped; models ranked training-set metrics . Expect 2 models leaderboard. Use quick sanity checks interactive exploration. 30–120s: baseline models attempted including random forest. Cross-validation runs enough time remains model fit; otherwise training metrics used. Advanced models (SVM, XGBoost / ridge, lasso) attempted 40\ remains baselines. Dimensionality reduction clustering pipelines run enabled 10\ 120s+ (recommended): full pipeline runs – baselines, advanced models, PCA-augmented variants, cluster-augmented variants, cross-validation. Expect 9–11 models leaderboard. individual model fits (especially forest, SVM, XGBoost CV) can take 5–30s depending data size, actual wall-clock time may modestly exceed budget duration last model started budget expired. cv_folds Number cross-validation folds (default: 5). Reducing (e.g. 2 3) effective way stay closer time budget since CV typically expensive step. metric Evaluation metric (default: auto-selected based task). classification: "accuracy"; regression: "rmse".

title: Create a tidylearn model — tl_model
text: Unified interface creating machine learning models wrapping established R packages. function dispatches appropriate underlying package based method.

title: Create a tidylearn model — tl_model
code: tl_model(data, formula = NULL, method = "linear", ..., compute = "cpu")

title: Create a tidylearn model — tl_model
text: data data frame containing training data formula formula specifying model. unsupervised methods, use ~ vars NULL. method modeling method. Supervised: "linear" (stats::lm), "logistic" (stats::glm), "tree" (rpart), "forest" (randomForest), "boost" (gbm), "ridge"/"lasso"/"elastic_net" (glmnet), "svm" (e1071), "nn" (nnet), "deep" (keras), "xgboost" (xgboost). method response agree, mismatch error rather meaningless fit: "linear" "polynomial" need numeric response, "logistic" needs exactly two classes, every supervised method takes either. Unsupervised: "pca" (stats::prcomp), "mds" (stats/MASS/smacof), "kmeans" (stats::kmeans), "pam"/"clara" (cluster), "hclust" (stats::hclust), "dbscan" (dbscan). ... Additional arguments passed underlying model function compute Compute tier fit. One "cpu" (default, existing behaviour), "gpu" (route local CUDA method upstream GPU path – xgboost deep learning today), "auto" (consult tl_compute_advisor pick per call), "cloud" (reserved – yet wired ). "gpu" requested method without upstream GPU path machine without detected GPU, call falls back CPU warning.

title: Create a tidylearn model — tl_model
text: tidylearn_model object (S3) containing fitted model ($fit, $fit$model unsupervised method), model specification ($spec), training data ($data). object also inherits method-specific class (e.g., tidylearn_linear) paradigm class (tidylearn_supervised tidylearn_unsupervised).

title: Create a tidylearn model — tl_model
text: wrapped packages include: stats (lm, glm, prcomp, kmeans, hclust), glmnet, randomForest, xgboost, gbm, e1071, nnet, rpart, cluster, dbscan. underlying algorithms unchanged - function provides consistent interface returns tidy output. supervised method, model$fit object wrapped function returned. unsupervised method returns tidied components well, wrapped object sits model$fit$model model$fit list holding . classification, response reduced classes actually contains: subsetting data frame keeps every factor level, level row uses otherwise reported class, given (zero) probability column, counted deciding whether problem binary. fit unaffected.

title: tidylearn 0.3.1
text: Column ranges (max - min) ordinal rank vectors previously recomputed every (, j) pair. now computed pre-pass, reducing work O(n² × p) O(n² + p). Replaced scalar data-frame indexing data[, k] — dispatches R-level [.data.frame method every call — pre-extracted plain-vector access col_vecs[[k]][], resolves C level. Benchmarks show 10–100× faster scalar access; gain compounds across full n*(n-1)/2 * p iterations. Column types (.numeric, .ordered) now resolved col_type character vector, removing repeated S3 predicate calls inner loop.

title: tidylearn 0.3.1
text: Fixed tl_reduce_dimensions() returning internal .obs_id row identifier column $data result. Passing data supervised model via response ~ . formula fed .obs_id high-cardinality predictor, made tree-based fits effectively non-terminating. identifier now dropped returned data, consistent pipeline transfer-learning paths already handle . Fixed print() summary() erroring model objects returned tl_step_selection() tl_tune_xgboost(). constructed object without spec$paradigm field tidylearn_supervised class, print method hit zero-length condition summary() took unsupervised branch. objects now built consistently tl_model(). Fixed tidy_gower() (tidy_dist(..., method = "gower")) erroring single-row input. pairwise loop used 1:(n - 1), produces invalid sequence 1:0 n 1; now uses seq_len(n - 1), single-row data frame returns empty dist object, consistent stats::dist().

text: Fixed tl_transfer_learning() hanging indefinitely used PCA pre-training. .obs_id row-identifier column PCA output included supervised formula, creating massive dummy-variable matrix. column now stripped training prediction. Fixed tl_run_pipeline() failing “attempt select less one element” cross-validation metrics NA. Root cause: scale() returned matrix columns instead vectors, causing downstream metric computation produce NaN. Added .vector() wrapper hardened best-model selection handle -NA metric values gracefully. Overhauled tl_auto_ml() time budget enforcement. budget now controls models attempted: budgets 30s skip slow C-level models (forest, SVM, XGBoost) entirely, cross-validation skipped remaining time tight. Baseline model order changed fast-first (tree, logistic/linear, forest). See ?tl_auto_ml full details budget tiers.

title: tidylearn 0.3.0
text: Fixed tl_interaction_effects() crashing “unused argument (se.fit)” tidylearn’s predict() method support se.fit. Now uses stats::predict() raw model object confidence intervals. Also fixed invalid formula internal slope calculation. Fixed tl_plot_interaction() expecting fit/lwr/upr columns predict() output. Now correctly handles tidylearn’s .pred tibble format.

title: tidylearn 0.3.0
text: Fixed tl_plot_intervals() calling non-existent tl_prediction_intervals() function. Now computes confidence prediction intervals directly via stats::predict(..., interval = "confidence") stats::predict(..., interval = "prediction"). Fixed tl_plot_svm_boundary() erroring “least two predictor variables required” using response ~ . formulas. function now resolves predictors data column names instead .vars(), expand .. Also switched geom_contour_filled (failed discrete class predictions) geom_raster. Fixed tl_plot_svm_tuning() passing NULL entries ranges list e1071::tune(), caused “NA/NaN/Inf foreign function call” errors. Tuning ranges now built conditionally based kernel type. Fixed tl_plot_xgboost_shap_summary() failing “arguments imply differing number rows” n_samples differed nrow(data). Sampling now performed SHAP computation feature values SHAP values always number rows.

title: tidylearn 0.3.0

Fixed SVM default gamma calculation use predictor count (1 / (ncol(data) - 1)) instead including response column. Added missing @return tag print.tidylearn_data().
